verdictStatement: The redesign is the best answer this lineage has produced to the question it has been circling since v8. Removing pendingTerminalizerRecord entirely and keeping order in the one journal via a reserved terminal-marker slot dissolves my v9 swallow hole rather than patching it: there is no external record left to lose, a terminalizer is either durably ordered or it is a retryable refusal outside the FIRST-wins set, and recovery is forbidden from reading an absent record as permission to resume. That is Codex's SCC-V9-B1 and B2 answered clause for clause. carrierQuarantineRecord's class treatment is answered the other way and equally well — by showing the SC-OPS journaled/redacted/bounded rule is SATISFIED (cardinality is the bound, the crash-atomic write is the audit, no secrets are stored) rather than displaced, with an explicit disclaimer that it does not inherit the grant journal's sequence exception. My FC-RO residue item is fixed and now matches the placement set exactly at six. The blocker is a single sentence the removal left behind. terminalization.capacityPauseIsNotFailClosedNoAppend still reads 'A terminalizer that arrives during the pause is stored as pendingTerminalizerRecord, not swallowed' — naming a byte-set this generation deleted from bytePlacement, in a live-normative field, directly contradicting the capacityPause clause four keys away that says no such record exists. Every other mention of that record in the artifact is correctly historical. This one is not.

blockers.title: A live-normative clause still directs terminalizers into pendingTerminalizerRecord — a byte-set this generation deleted and does not place — contradicting the capacityPause rule in the same object
blockers.subjectQuote: capacityPause is not a failClosedNoAppend state. See lifecycle.capacityPause. A terminalizer that arrives during the pause is stored as pendingTerminalizerRecord, not swallowed.

measurement.theRecordIsGone: I enumerated bytePlacement: 14 entries, none named pendingTerminalizerRecord (v9 had 15 including it). The removal is deliberate and declared — /basedOn/method's roster parenthetical reads '(remove pendingTerminalizerRecord; …)' and /honestyRepairsFromV9[0] states 'pendingTerminalizerRecord is removed.'
measurement.theContradictionIsInTheSameObject: Four keys away in the same lifecycle, capacityPause states 'There is no external pending-terminalizer record and no second ordering authority.' The two clauses cannot both be followed.
measurement.everyOtherMentionIsHistorical: I walked every string in the artifact for the term. Seven occurrences: /basedOn/method (declares the removal), /honestyRepairsFromV8[0] and /honestyRepairsFromV9[0] and [2] (succession history), /proposedSupersession/whyNotSilent (history), /reviewGuidance[40] (an append-only attack instruction). All six of those are correctly historical. EXACTLY ONE is live-normative — this clause — and it is the only one that describes the deleted mechanism as current design.
measurement.itReinstatesTheBlockedDesign: SCC-V9-B1's title was 'pendingTerminalizerRecord is a second durable ordering authority outside the sole grant journal.' The mechanism was removed to answer it, but the sentence that describes storing terminalizers in that record survives. On the bytes as they stand, the contract still says a terminalizer is stored in an external record.
measurement.itMandatesAnUnplacedDurableByte: The clause names a durable byte-set with no class, no owner, no sole writer and no lifecycle anywhere in bytePlacement. That is the condition DR-124 exists to eliminate, and P-002-4 — carried in this artifact's own whatIsSuperseded as remaining in force — states that DR-124 'must assign every persisted byte one class, owner, writer, and lifecycle before blueprint work.'
measurement.theRosterDidNotPreventIt: /bytePlacement is on the closed roster and the terminalization object sits beneath it, so this clause was editable this generation and simply was not edited. The roster claim itself is not violated: I measured 54 changed paths with zero off-roster and 198 of 198 non-roster paths identical.

blockers.whyBlocker: A coordinator recording v10 would record a contract whose live text still routes terminalizers into a second durable store — the exact thing Codex's v9 blocker was raised about and the exact thing this generation removed. The defect is not ambiguity a reader can resolve by preferring the newer clause; it is a normative sentence naming an unplaced byte-set, inside the one artifact whose subject is that every durable byte-set be placed. It also sits on the safety property at issue: 'not swallowed' is now guaranteed by the reserved-slot mechanism, and attributing it instead to a record that does not exist leaves the guarantee resting on nothing. The artifact's own reviewGuidance entry 40 invites precisely this attack — 'Attack a pending-terminalizer record that is still a second ordering authority' — and the attack lands.
blockers.whatIsNotWrong: The design is right and I am not asking for any of it to change. The reserved-slot answer is better than the no-drop property I proposed at v9, the retryable-refusal rule is correct, and carrierQuarantineRecord's satisfaction argument is well made. This is a deletion that did not reach one sentence, not a design error.
blockers.minimumRepair: Rewrite the third sentence of terminalization.capacityPauseIsNotFailClosedNoAppend to match capacityPause: a terminalizer arriving during the pause is accepted only when the reserved grant-journal terminal-marker is durably appended, and is otherwise a retryable refusal outside the FIRST-wins set — with no external record. Since the first two sentences already delegate ('See lifecycle.capacityPause'), deleting the third sentence outright would also resolve it. Then re-check that no other live-normative field names a removed mechanism; I found no second instance, so this is a one-sentence edit.

attacksAttemptedAndFailed.attack: A reserved-slot failure that still counts as FIRST (dispatch and subject attack surface)
attacksAttemptedAndFailed.result: FAILED. capacityPause is explicit: acceptance requires the reserved marker to be durably appended, and 'If the reserved append cannot be completed, the terminalizer is a retryable refusal and is NOT a member of the FIRST-wins set.' I could not construct an ordering in which an incomplete append is treated as the winning terminalizer.

attacksAttemptedAndFailed.attack: A pending-terminalizer record that is still a second ordering authority (dispatch and subject attack surface)
attacksAttemptedAndFailed.result: FAILED as a mechanism — the record is removed from bytePlacement and order is kept in the single journal. It survives only as a sentence, which is B-1. I distinguish the two deliberately: the design has no second ordering authority; the text still describes one.

attacksAttemptedAndFailed.attack: carrierQuarantineRecord is still an unauthorized departure from the SC-OPS bounded rule (my v9 B-1 limb one, re-run)
attacksAttemptedAndFailed.result: FAILED, and I withdrew it on measurement. The record now answers the file 04 rule term by term — journaled (its crash-atomic write is the audit), redacted (no VALUES or HANDLES), bounded (exactly one current record per carrier; that cardinality is the bound) — and expressly disclaims inheriting SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL's sequence-journal displacement. Showing the rule is satisfied is a complete answer to the authority question; no supersession extension is needed.

attacksAttemptedAndFailed.attack: Removing the record reopened the swallow hole in a new form — a terminalizer lost because it was never recorded anywhere
attacksAttemptedAndFailed.result: FAILED. A terminalizer is only ever accepted by becoming a durable journal record; anything short of that is an explicit refusal the caller can retry. There is no window in which an accepted terminalizer exists outside the journal, so there is nothing to lose. Recovery is separately forbidden from reading an absent external record as permission to resume.

coordinatorNote: One blocker, one sentence wide, and I want the shape of it clear because it would be easy to over- or under-read. The design this generation ships is the strongest version of the grant-journal lifecycle so far: removing the external pending record and putting the terminal transition into a reserved slot in the one journal answers both Codex blockers and my own at their root, and carrierQuarantineRecord's class treatment is now argued rather than asserted. I found nothing wrong with any of it and no SHOULD-FIX anywhere in the artifact. What survives is a sentence describing the mechanism that was deleted, sitting in a live-normative field and contradicting the clause that replaced it. It matters because it names a durable byte-set with no placement — the one condition this row exists to eliminate — and because it is textually the second ordering authority Codex blocked at v9. Deleting that sentence, or restating it in capacityPause's terms, resolves it; nothing else needs to move. If it helps the next round, OBS-2 suggests adding a removed-identifier sweep to the roster check, since the mechanical diff proves what changed but not what still refers to what is gone. I did not read the other current v10 reviewer, did not edit the subject or the prompt, did not edit file 08 or COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, did not apply SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL, did not mint a D-096 (A) grant, did not mark any DR SATISFIED, and did not commit.
